maxim: all things are now lawful to you in jack feist
scope: A THREE-PIECE DEMONSTRATION, not the whole volume. PEARL, Undersong II: the metaphor factory, and Johannes Sigil's appendix essay. Built to test whether a relationship can carry its own evidence before the design is extended across 42 pieces.
why:
The inventory made pieces addressable and stopped there. A relation of the form essay -> PEARL says almost nothing: it does not say WHICH PASSAGE, on what evidence, asserted by whom, or whether it is an explicit reference or a proposed reading. A CLASSIFICATION IS NOT A RELATIONSHIP.

Here every relation names two passages, carries the text that grounds it, and states who asserted it — the text itself, or a named voice inside the book.
the_finding:
THE LINE 'and moons no longer walk the earth.' STANDS TWICE, VERBATIM — in PEARL and again in UNDERSONG II: THE METAPHOR FACTORY. An undersong repeats a line of the poem it undersings.

AND SIGIL'S ESSAY QUOTES IT ONCE, attributing it to 'Pearl' — which is true of the first occurrence and silent about the second. The essay's title claims to develop 'Some Themes Introduced in Lee Sharks' Pearl'; its quotations are drawn from PEARL and its undersongs together, which is a claim about where a poem's themes are introduced that the essay makes by practice rather than by argument.
